sections.html:
Three separate offices touch a Tipton County tax bill. The Assessor values every parcel. The county commission and each city council set rates. The Trustee mails the bills and takes the money. The Assessor's office does not set the rate, send bills or collect taxes.

The Trustee works from 1 Pleasant Avenue, Room 203, in Covington (mailing address PO Box 487, Covington, TN 38019), phone 901-476-0211, weekdays 8:00 to 5:00. During tax season a second counter opens at Munford City Hall, 1397 Munford Avenue, every Wednesday from the first Wednesday in October through February 24, 2027, with a few holiday dates skipped. Questions about value or a mailing address go to the Assessor at 901-476-0213.

City tax is separate. City taxes are not collected at the county counter, so use the municipal offices:

  • Covington, 200 W Washington Avenue, 901-476-9613
  • Atoka, 334 Atoka-Munford Avenue, 901-837-5300
  • Brighton, 1270 Old Highway 51 S, 901-476-8661
  • Mason, 12157 Main Street, 901-294-3525
  • Munford, 1397 Munford Avenue, 901-837-0171

Covington sets its own due date at October 1 and its delinquency date at March 1, refuses partial payments, and charges a city rate of $1.0128 for each $100 of assessed value. A Covington house therefore carries a county bill and a city bill.

Tipton County lies on the western edge of Tennessee along the Mississippi River, with Covington as the county seat, and it belongs to the Memphis metro area. U.S. Highway 51 runs north to south through Covington. The county sits on the southeastern edge of the New Madrid Seismic Zone, an area of high earthquake risk, which is a fair question to raise with an insurer. Covington's South Main Historic District keeps about 50 homes from the late 1800s and early 1900s, and the district is federally registered.

Population was 62,287 in July 2025, up 2.2% since April 2020. There are 25,033 housing units, and 76.3% of occupied ones are owned by their residents. A typical owned home is worth $240,600, and typical rent is $1,013. Only 139 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction competes lightly with resale homes.

The Assessor sets an appraised value, the state assessment ratio turns that into assessed value, and the rate is applied per $100. The ratios are residential 25 percent, farm 25 percent, commercial and industrial 40 percent, personal property 30 percent, and public utility 55 percent. The 2026 county rate is $1.3417 per $100, down from $1.5217 in 2025. The rate has fallen steadily in the history the Trustee posts:

Tipton County is on a six-year reappraisal cycle: five years of on-site review of every parcel, then a revaluation in the sixth year. Ask the Assessor which year of the cycle the county is in, since a revaluation year is when the value of a house tends to move most.

sections.h2: Due dates, interest and ways to pay
sections.html:
Billing opens on the first Monday in October, and the interest-free period runs through the last day of February. On March 1 the account is delinquent. The Trustee then adds 1.5 percent on the first of each month and rounds to the nearest dollar. The schedule reads 1.5 percent in March, 3.0 in April and 4.5 in May, reaching 18.0 percent in February of the following year and 19.5 in March.

The notice leaves the office in the first week of October, addressed to the January 1 owner. The Trustee takes payment in these ways:

  • At the Covington counter, or at the Wednesday Munford counter during the season
  • Online through the Trustee's payment portal, where the vendor adds 2.5 percent on a card or $1.25 on an online check
  • By phone at 1-855-548-3603, with a $0.30 processing fee on top of the vendor charges
  • By bank draft, either in one annual payment, in four payments from November to February, or monthly, arranged at 901-476-0211

Partial payments are welcome, but interest is added to whatever remains after February 28. A refund is only issued on a parcel that another agency, such as a lender, has already paid. No other reason qualifies.

A Tipton County owner who thinks the roll overstates a house has two steps. First comes the local County Board of Equalization. The Assessor posts the roll for public viewing in May and mails notices on parcels whose value moved, and the board's ruling closes out the roll for that year. Second comes the state equalization board, which takes a filing up to August 1, or 45 days after the local notice went out, whichever is later. Read the date printed on your notice.

Facts and numbers carry a hearing. The state's guidance names three kinds of proof:

  • Recent sales of look-alike homes nearby, with adjustments for size, age and condition
  • A written appraisal from a professional who is ready to testify
  • Your own figure for the value, backed by reasons

Pay the part of the tax you do not dispute before March 1, along with any older delinquent tax. The State Board's phone line is 615-401-7883.

The state reimburses part or all of the tax for low-income elderly and disabled homeowners, disabled former service members, and their widowed spouses. The program dates to 1973. The Trustee's 2026 income cap is $38,470 from every source, for the applicant, spouse and any other owner, measured on 2025 income. Because it is a reimbursement and not an exemption, the bill is paid first.

Paperwork differs by group. Elderly applicants bring 2025 income proof and a Medicare or Social Security card. Disabled applicants bring proof of age plus a benefits letter when the payer is not Social Security. Disabled former service members sign an F-16 and show ID. Mobile home owners add a title, bill of sale or affidavit of affixation. The office begins the 2026 process in October, so call 901-476-0211 to book.

The January 1 owner is on the roll, so a house sold in the fall still carries a bill in the seller's name. At closing the title company normally splits the year, and the buyer takes over from there. If you owe tax, ask the Trustee for the exact payoff, including any interest, before setting a closing date. Interest climbs each month after February, so a quick closing, including a cash sale that skips lender delays, limits how much extra you pay.

Gather these before you call: the parcel number, the name on the notice, and the date you hope to close. If the house is inside Covington, Atoka, Brighton, Mason or Munford, ask that city's office for a separate figure, because the Trustee does not collect city tax.

faqs.q: What rate applies to a Tipton County house in 2026?
faqs.a: The 2026 county rate is $1.3417 for each $100 of assessed value, lower than the $1.5217 charged in 2025. City tax is billed separately, and Covington lists $1.0128 per $100.

faqs.q: How long can I wait to pay Tipton County tax before interest begins?
faqs.a: The last interest-free day is February 28. Billing opens on the first Monday in October, and each month after that date adds 1.5 percent.

faqs.q: Where can I hand over a Tipton County tax payment?
faqs.a: Pay at the Trustee's office at 1 Pleasant Avenue, Room 203, in Covington, or on Wednesdays at Munford City Hall during tax season. Online, phone and bank draft payments are also offered.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund of Tipton County property tax?
faqs.a: Only on a parcel that another agency has already paid, such as a lender. Refunds are not issued for any other reason.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Tipton County Assessor?
faqs.a: The Assessor's line is 901-476-0213. That office can talk through a value and explain how to get on the county board's schedule.
